author: original (NevaIB)
title: Measures of centre and spread

points.text: Mean, median and mode; estimating a mean from grouped data; modal class
IQR, standard deviation and variance (by GDC)
Effect of adding or multiplying all data by a constant

bigPicture: Centre and spread summarise a data set in two numbers. Know when each measure is appropriate and how they change when every value is transformed.

keyIdeas.cue: Mean, median, mode; how do you estimate the mean of grouped data?
keyIdeas.answer: Mean = total ÷ number; median = middle value; mode = most frequent. Grouped data: use class midpoints, x̄ ≈ Σfx/Σf; the modal class has the highest frequency.

keyIdeas.cue: Which measures of spread, and how are they found?
keyIdeas.answer: IQR = Q3 − Q1 (resistant to outliers). Standard deviation σ measures typical distance from the mean; variance = σ². Find σ on the GDC (one-variable statistics).

keyIdeas.cue: Effect of adding or multiplying every value by a constant?
keyIdeas.answer: Adding k: mean, median and quartiles increase by k; standard deviation, variance and IQR do not change. Multiplying by k: mean and σ are multiplied by k (k > 0), variance by k².
Q1 is the median of the lower half and Q3 the median of the upper half (excluding the median when n is odd). GDCs may use slightly different methods.

keyTerms.def: typical distance of data from the mean
the class with the highest frequency

misconceptions.wrong: Adding 5 to every value adds 5 to the standard deviation

misconceptions.right: It is an estimate, because midpoints replace the real values.

practice.prompt: (a) The mean of five numbers is 12. A sixth number x is added and the mean becomes 13. Find x. (b) A data set has mean 20 and standard deviation 4. Each value is multiplied by 3 and then 5 is added. Find the new mean and standard deviation.
Using the grouped masses in the worked example, use the GDC to estimate the standard deviation.
solution: enter midpoints in L1 and frequencies in L2
